findings.F1: Below the SMA200 the coin's excess 10-day return is only slightly negative, mean -0.0034 (t -0.70, n 841 non-overlapping blocks), against +0.0037 (t 0.61, n 816) above it, and the plan's allocation × excess product stays near zero at every horizon (10 days: -0.00027, t -0.23; 3 to 40 days: |t| ≤ 0.41). The effect is weak overall.
findings.F2: The effect is mixed across periods and cancels out. Below the SMA200 the excess 10-day return is clearly negative in the bear years: 2018 -0.0395 (t -2.41, n 137), 2019 -0.0158 (t -1.87) and 2022 -0.0250 (t -2.64, n 191). It is clearly positive in the recovery years: 2020 +0.0493 (t 3.05, n 73), 2021 +0.0416 (t 1.75) and 2023 +0.0190 (t 1.67).
findings.F3: The test's grading runs against the effect. The deepest forecast quartile is followed by a rise, excess +0.0076 (t 0.71, n 211), while the shallow quartile falls, -0.0080 (t -0.84). The deepest distance bin (-72% to -36.5%) averages -0.0001 against -0.0068 for the shallowest bin. The slope of excess return on allocation is -0.0126, so the clipped standardised forecast puts its largest shorts where falls stop.
findings.F4: The fall shows where the 200-day average itself is falling fastest. The quartile with the steepest 20-day decline of the SMA200 has excess 10-day return -0.0175 (t -1.66, n 173, 54% of blocks down), against -0.0012 (t -0.11) for the quartile where it rises most. Over 20 days the same split gives -0.0159 against +0.0153.
findings.F5: The coin's recent path splits the outcome. Below the SMA200, a high 30-day return (top quartile) is followed by excess -0.0159 over 10 days (t -1.55, n 154). The lowest 30-day return is followed by +0.0064 over 10 days and +0.0479 over 20 days (t 1.58, n 67): bounces under a falling average fail, and sharp drops rebound.
findings.F6: Time spent below the average is mixed too. Excess 10-day return is -0.0185 (t -1.71) in the first 10 days below, +0.0191 (t 1.93) at 11–30 days and -0.0167 (t -1.81) after 60 days. This adds to the mixed picture rather than giving one clean side.

ideas.idea: While the coin's close is below its 200-day simple moving average, it keeps falling beyond its usual drift over the next 10 days, the more so the faster that 200-day average has itself declined over the past 20 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short coins below their long average only when the average itself is turning down steeply, and size up with the steepness of that decline rather than with the distance below it.
ideas.name: falling-average downside persistence

ideas.idea: While the coin's close is below its 200-day simple moving average, it falls beyond its usual drift over the next 10 days, the more so the higher its 30-day return has been.
ideas.consequence: A trader would sell rallies that happen beneath the long average, and refuse to short a coin that has just dropped hard below it.
ideas.name: failed rally below average

ideas.idea: The further a coin's close sits below its 200-day simple moving average and the more it has fallen over the past 30 days, the more it rises beyond its usual drift over the next 20 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat deep, fresh drops under the long average as rebound candidates rather than as short signals.
ideas.name: deep drop rebound
